headline: Frozen on 10 October 2026: United's third-quarter adjusted EPS is put at $2.54 a share (P10 $2.18, P90 $2.82) against its own range of $2.50 to $3.50, with fuel at $3.93 a gallon instead of the $3.69 United assumed.
plain_summary: Frozen on 10 October 2026: United's third-quarter adjusted EPS is put at $2.54 a share (P10 $2.18, P90 $2.82) against its own range of $2.50 to $3.50, with fuel at $3.93 a gallon instead of the $3.69 United assumed.

Fuel: the cost clock puts the price United paid at $3.93 a gallon (P10 $3.87, P90 $4.00); United assumed about $3.69 on 15 July 2026. The gap is $297 million before tax, or $0.58 a share after tax and profit sharing.

Recovery: 21% of that gap is expected back through revenue within the quarter (P10 6%, P90 27%). United said it expects to recover 80% to 90% of the fuel increase in the quarter, but never defined 'recover', so the two figures are not the same measure.
Unit revenue: up 14.7% on a year earlier (P10 11.1%, P90 17.5%); United said more than 12.1%. This link does not feed the EPS figure.
EPS: $3.00 midpoint less $0.46 of fuel cost not recovered gives $2.54. Applying each of United's 14 earlier misses against its own midpoint, 7 land below the guided range, 6 inside and 1 above.
Against the $2.84 analyst consensus read on 10 October 2026, 1 of the 14 values is higher (7%); a thinly traded prediction market put the chance of a result above $2.84 at 60%.

How this method did on the 10 quarters from 2024 to mid-2026: average miss $0.26 a share, against $0.26 for United's own midpoint and $0.26 for costs only. It did not beat the midpoint there, so this call is a test of the method, not a claim that it is better than United's own number.
The forecast block is fixed: its SHA-256 is in `sha256` and the same bytes are in data/lab/q3_call_frozen.json. The outcome and the scores are added beside it after United reports.
limits: One forecast, made once. It rests on the same few quarters as the track record: the method was chosen on 4 quarters and tested on 10, where it did not beat United's own midpoint on average miss.
The EPS range is the spread of United's earlier misses against its own midpoint, not a product of the link ranges. Those misses already contain past fuel and revenue surprises.
The odds are shares of 14 values, so they are coarse.

The fuel price is an estimate from Gulf Coast spot prices. United buys at many airports and the cost clock ran low in 15 of 18 past quarters even after refitting; the middle of those misses is shown but not added.
The same-quarter recovery share leans on one quarter, 2026Q2; `sensitivities` shows the call with two lower shares.

The consensus figure was read from the web by another part of the build and is not machine-checked; a search made for this forecast on the same day returned different figures from other providers. The prediction market is thinly traded.
Anything United said outside its SEC filings after 15 July 2026 is not in the inputs.
Profit sharing uses a rate read from a paraphrase; the call after tax only is in `without_profit_sharing`.
The unit revenue link uses coefficients fitted on the same quarters its range is drawn from and assumes capacity growth from April; it is a side forecast and does not feed the EPS figure.
sha256_of: the canonical JSON of `forecast` (sorted keys, separators ',' and ':', UTF-8); the same bytes are in data/lab/q3_call_frozen.json
timestamp_proof_note: Not created by the build. The file to stamp is data/lab/q3_call_frozen.json.
known_before_freeze: Delta reported its September quarter on 2026-10-09: adjusted EPS $1.72 against a guided $2.00 to $2.50; it paid $3.61 a gallon against an assumed $3.15; adjusted unit revenue rose 15% year over year. No Delta figure enters any number in this forecast.
Daily Gulf Coast jet fuel prices through 2026-09-30 for the quarter itself; the quarter ended on 2026-09-30, so its fuel prices are all known.
United's results through the second quarter of 2026, published on 2026-07-15.
No guidance update from United between 2026-07-16 and 2026-10-10 is in the committed filings (latest filing in the index: 2026-07-15).
Airport security counts for the quarter: travellers -2.8% against a year earlier (national, all airlines). Not an input to the forecast.

Analyst consensus for the quarter's EPS: $2.84, as read on 2026-10-10 (https://tickzen.app/stocks/ual/earnings). A prediction market priced a result above $2.84 at 60% on 2026-10-10, with about $690 traded in total. Neither enters any number in the chain.

chain.method: Cost clock refitted on every clean quarter reported before the quarter's end (26 quarters, latest report 2026-07-15), at the quarter's actual daily fuel prices. P10 and P90 are the estimate plus the 10th and 90th percentile of the clock's own misses on earlier quarters, each made with the clock as it stood at that quarter's end, less their middle value.

clock_own_range.note: The clock's own range from its regression error. It held the reported price in too few past quarters, so it is not used.

past_misses.note: Reported price minus the clock's estimate. The middle value is shown, not added to the P50: the replay did not add it either.

chain.unit: share of the fuel surprise recovered in the quarter

curve_same_quarter_share.note: p50 is the least-squares share for the quarter of a fuel change, the figure the replay uses (smooth.expanding in fare_clock.json). p10 and p90 are from the fare clock's resampled curves; their middle value is lower than the least-squares share because that share leans on one quarter, 2026Q2.

chain.definition: The published curve is recovery(k) = L x (1 - rho^(k+1)): L is the share of a lasting fuel cost change that unit revenue makes up in the long run, rho how much of the remaining gap stays open each quarter.
chain.management_note: United never defined 'recover'. Its 80% to 90% is a statement about the whole 2026 fuel increase in the third quarter, with no formula and no baseline. The management call applies it to the fuel surprise as it stands; the two shares are not the same measure.
chain.one_quarter_after_note: For the fuel increase that began in spring 2026 the third quarter is one quarter after the shock; this is the fare clock's share there, the closest like-for-like figure to United's statement.
chain.method: The chosen variant gives the curve's same-quarter share to the part of the surprise that had arrived by the middle of the quarter and nothing to the part that arrived later. p10, p50 and p90 are that share as a fraction of the whole surprise.

chain.form_description: one quarter ahead: last quarter's reported year-over-year change, plus the change in the fuel term and in the capacity term
chain.form_rule: The fare clock scored two forms of its equation; the one with the lower miss on 2020-2023 is used (1.76 against 3.64 cents per seat mile, in its own file).

range_from.note: The same form's misses on every earlier quarter with no pandemic level behind it, less their middle value. The curve's coefficients were fitted on those quarters, so the range is too narrow.

assumptions: Gallons burned per seat mile are the same as in the third quarter a year earlier.
Capacity growth is the middle of what United stated in April 2026; no later figure is in the guidance file.

odds.note: Shares of the 14 sample values: today's central estimate with each of United's 14 earlier misses against its midpoint applied in turn. With this few values the odds move in steps of 7 percentage points.

scoring.definition: CRPS of `eps_samples` against the adjusted diluted EPS United reports, in US dollars a share; for a single-number baseline CRPS is its absolute miss. Lower is better. The fuel price and unit revenue links are scored by absolute miss and by whether the outcome falls inside P10-P90.
scoring.consensus_note: The consensus baseline is the figure in `comparators`, fixed here before the report.

consensus_eps.provider_note: Tickzen, which says its estimates come from Yahoo Finance. It does not name the quarter ("the next report") or say whether the figure is adjusted.

also_stated_by.quote: The Street consensus estimate for United Airlines’s non-GAAP EPS for the relevant quarter is $2.84
also_stated_by.note: The threshold written into the prediction market below, which opened on 2026-10-07.

consensus_eps.read_via: page text returned by a web reader (a language model); wording not machine-checked
consensus_eps.caution: Read from the web by the meta builder, not machine-checked. A separate search made for this forecast on the same day returned different consensus figures from other providers; none of those is recorded.

target.measure: adjusted diluted EPS, as United reports it

method.variant_note: The same, but fuel that moved after the middle of the quarter (or after the guidance date, if later) is treated as not recovered at all in that quarter.
method.same_as_replay: tr.forecast: the function that produced every replayed quarter in track_record.json
method.selection_rule: Lowest average CRPS over the replayed quarters of 2013-2023; the plain fitted call keeps ties. Decided before any quarter from 2024 onward was scored, and identical whether or not those quarters are loaded.
method.fuel_effect_note: The closed-form chain from the replay, not the simulator: the simulator's first whole quarter is the fourth quarter of 2026. The simulator is run beside it as a cross-check.

updates_since.note: The index lists earnings releases and investor updates (Form 8-K items 2.02, 7.01 and 8.01) fetched on the build day. A statement made only in the press or at a conference would not be in it.

sensitivities.note: Not the forecast. The replay tried this correction on the quarters before 2024 and it scored worse there.

closed_form_chain.note: The chain's own figures for the third quarter, before profit sharing, for comparison.

simulator_cross_check.per_share_rule: tax rate 0.2154, 326.6 million diluted shares, no profit sharing
simulator_cross_check.note: Two simulator runs on the same 10,000 worlds that differ only in the fuel price level, held for three months. The simulator starts from United's business as of 2026-07-16 and its first whole quarter is the fourth quarter of 2026, so it cannot produce the third quarter; the forecast therefore uses the closed-form chain from the replay. `replay_curve` gives the simulator the same same-quarter share the chain uses (39%); `measured` draws from the fare clock's resampled curves, whose middle same-quarter share is lower.
